pr_body:
This has operations for the following:
1. create a changefeed to null sink with initial scan randomly set to yes or no or only.
2. pause one of the randomly selected changefeed
3. resume one of the randomly selected changefeed
4. cancel one of the randomly selected changefeed

If no changefeed jobs are running or paused, and any of cancel, pause or resume is invoked, it invoked create operation.

Please refer to https://cockroachlabs.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TE/pages/4267933701/CDC+Operation+for+CREATE+PAUSE+RESUME+CANCEL

All configurations are environment variables. This can be later changed to be in a configuration file.

Fixes: #138477 #138480 #138481 #138475 
Epic: None
Release Note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/140582)

> Nice work putting this together! I think it could be simplified a bit, since it will be easier to reason about simpler operations in the future.
> 
> One thing I wonder is that if we call pause, resume, or cancel operations when there are no changefeeds running, if we should create a changefeed instead. What do you think?

Thanks @rharding6373 and @asg0451  for reviewing the changes. I am still working on few changes and will let you know when it is ready for review again.
Regarding, calling create from pause, resume or cancel, that can be done. We need to add some extra checks like, currently we query for only paused jobs to resume. If the query returns 0, we exit. Now, we need to check for all running and paused jobs and if that is 0, then we call create. Not a big task, but wanted to highlight. Let me know if that sound ok.
@rharding6373 @asg0451 , I have made the changes as mentioned. PTAL. Thanks!
Thanks @asg0451 for your review. I have made the changes. PTAL.

review_comments: I don't think we need the `createOnlyIfNoJobs` parameter. In the only path where it's true, we already checked that `fetchAllChangefeedJobsWithStates` returned 0 jobs, so it's unnecessary.
In case of RESUME, this is not the case if there are jobs in RUNNING state. So the first query returns 0 jobs to resume. Same with PAUSE.
can't you just use the return value of the `CREATE CHANGEFEED` statement? that's the job id
I tried using the `result.LastInsertId()`, but, it did not give me the JOB ID.
I will be merging this PR and we will take this up when the sink changes are worked on.
